meta.method: 38 WebSearch/WebFetch calls (15 EN, 7 KO, 7 ES, 9 fetch/verify); Reddit not used. Search-engine AI summaries were treated as secondary and flagged where the underlying page could not be fetched.
meta.budget_note: Exceeded the ~25-call guideline (38 used) in an attempt to verify the single LA-specific mode-split figure; verification still failed (see evidence id 4 and gaps).

evidence.claim: "Two Wheels, One Big Shift: 2026 Two-Wheeled Progress Report" (Mar 18, 2026): the number of deliveries on two-wheeled devices grew nearly four times faster than car-based deliveries across the U.S. and Canada between 2024 and 2025, "led by cities in the Bay Area like San Francisco and Santa Clara." "Dashers in the U.S. and Canada on two-wheels earned on average over 10% more per hour spent on the app than those delivering by car" and "spent around 15% less time traveling from offer acceptance to store arrival for pickup." The fetched report text contains NO Los Angeles figure.
evidence.geography: US/Canada (national); Bay Area named; LA not mentioned in fetched text
evidence.quant: two-wheel deliveries grew ~4x faster than car 2024->2025; +10% $/hr; -15% time to pickup

evidence.claim: DoorDash 2025 report (Feb 25, 2025, 2024 data) defines two-wheeled devices as "bicycle, e-bike, scooter, or moped" and gives city shares: Washington DC 57%, Philadelphia 35%, Toronto 32%, Boston 32%. "In the top 20 cities for deliveries, Dashers using two-wheeled devices earned about 10 percent more than Dashers using cars." Dashers traveled over 40 million miles on two-wheeled devices during a four-week period. No Los Angeles figure in the fetched text.
evidence.geography: US/Canada; DC, Philadelphia, Toronto, Boston cited; LA absent
evidence.quant: DC 57%, PHL 35%, TOR 32%, BOS 32% (2024); definition includes scooter/moped

evidence.claim: Silicon Valley Bicycle Coalition summarizing DoorDash's 2026 report: in Santa Clara and Sunnyvale "approximately 75% of all DoorDash deliveries in 2025 were completed on two wheels." Search-result snippets from the same report cluster state San Francisco stands at 72%. No Los Angeles sentence in the article.
evidence.geography: Santa Clara / Sunnyvale / San Francisco (comparators only)
evidence.source: Silicon Valley Bicycle Coalition (secondary, citing DoorDash)

evidence.claim: UNVERIFIED: a search-engine AI summary of the result set for the 2026 DoorDash report asserted "Los Angeles reached 49% of DoorDash deliveries completed on two wheels in 2025 ... lags behind Santa Clara and Sunnyvale (75%) and San Francisco (72%)." The 49% figure did NOT appear in the fetched text of the DoorDash 2026 report, the DoorDash 2025 report, or the SVBC article; a targeted search for DoorDash + "Los Angeles" + "49%" returned no page containing it. Candidate primary carriers (Axios 2025-02-25 city map; Axios San Diego 2026-03-19; micromobility.io) returned HTTP 403; Zag Daily returned empty. Treat as a lead to confirm, not as evidence.
evidence.source: Search-engine summary only (no page confirmed); candidate sources: micromobility.io, Axios

evidence.claim: Axios San Diego headline (page returned 403, title only): "About one third of DoorDash deliveries in San Diego use bikes." Consistent with the ~30% San Diego figure in the brief; the article reportedly carries per-city figures from the 2026 DoorDash report and is the most likely place an LA number would appear.
evidence.source: Axios San Diego (headline only; body not fetched)

evidence.claim: Axios published a DoorDash bicycle-delivery city map (Feb 25, 2025, 2024 data) — HTTP 403 on fetch; content not extracted. Likely contains a 2024 LA two-wheel share.

DoorDash Dasher Central bike-dashing page: "Bike dashing helps you save money, beat traffic, and deliver faster in busy cities... Bike Dashers can earn up to 10% more than Dashers who drive in urban areas." "During the sign-up process, you just need to select 'Bicycle' as your mode of transport. If dashing via bike only, you'll need a driver's license or other form of ID." Third-party summaries add that bike dashing "is available in select cities" and "most large cities allow you to sign up... using a bike"; no LA-specific city list published.
evidence.source: DoorDash Dasher Central (primary) + Financial Panther summary

evidence.claim: DoorDash Help Center, "Can I dash on a bike, scooter, or by walking?": "Depending on your local market, you may be able to use scooters or bikes to dash." No city list; no mention of a motorcycle dash type; walking not confirmed in fetched text.

DoorDash Help Center on dash types (via search summary): "You can add a bike, scooter, or car, and choose whichever fits your dash before you start"; to dash by scooter go to vehicle management > add new vehicle > scooter; "You are required to go through a vehicle background check to be able to sign up for a scooter. Bikes and e-bikes don't require a driver's license to dash. Many scooters and mopeds require a driver's license." Dasher Central blog 'Bike vs. Car vs. Scooter': "two-wheeled Dashers earned on average over 10% more per hour than Dashers using cars in the top 20 U.S. cities" (LA is a top-20 market).
evidence.source: DoorDash Help Center + Dasher Central blog (primary, via summary)

evidence.claim: Uber Eats LA courier page: "You can get around Los Angeles by car, scooter, or bike to pick up orders." Requirements per mode (driversnote summary of Uber policy): car — 19+, license, 2-door+ vehicle; scooter — "at least 19 years old, have a valid driver's license, and your motorized scooter must have an engine size below 50cc"; bike — 18+, state ID; on foot — 18+, government ID. Uber explicitly offers all four modes in LA.

Uber Spanish-language LA page, "Conviértete en repartidor en Los Ángeles, CA": "Puedes hacer entregas en tu auto, bicicleta, scooter o, incluso, a pie." "Antes de aceptar un pedido, podrás ver cuánto recibirás por hacer la entrega."
Job aggregator listing: "Los Angeles Job: Ubereats Bicycle & Scooter Courier (No Exp Req*) | Uber" — Uber recruiting ads in LA are explicitly segmented for bicycle/scooter couriers.

Third-party Spanish support site: DoorDash "facilita el trabajo de reparto con bicicletas, motocicletas o vehículos y acepta ITIN"; Uber Eats scooter rule repeated in Spanish (19+, licencia, scooter <50cc, SSN). Frames app delivery for immigrant workers as bici/moto/auto.

Spanish-language TikTok discover pages aggregate courier earnings videos: "Cómo Hacer Delivery En Estados Unidos En Bicicleta", "Cuanto Gana Un Delivery En Moto En Estados Unidos", "Cuanto Gana Un Repartidor De Uber Eats En Bicicleta"; one creator reports "$27.75 USD in less than an hour" on a bike (city unspecified). @delivery.tv video "Cómo hacer entregas en bicicleta con Doordash y Uber Eats" (2022). No LA-specific moto/bici vlog with channel, date and $/hr was extractable from the tool.

English TikTok discover page "How to Start Uber Eats on A Bike Los Angeles" aggregates clips showing e-bike delivery for DoorDash/Uber Eats in LA including Downtown LA (DTLA). Individual channel/date/$ not extractable via tool.

Zoomo US page (surfaced by Spanish query): "Uber Eats riders get e-bikes for just $20/week" incl. U-lock, GPS, 6-hour battery, free repairs, phone mount. Rideshare Guy: Zoomo partners with Uber Eats, DoorDash, Deliveroo. Zoomo's current LA availability was not confirmed in this pass.

Whizz (courier e-bike subscription) lists its markets as NYC, San Francisco, Washington DC, Philadelphia, Chicago and Jersey City — Los Angeles is NOT among them. Indicates thin dedicated courier e-bike rental supply in LA relative to SF/NYC.

DoorDash and Intersection took "1,400 bikes and 220 docking stations in L.A. Metro's Bike Share Program with Exclusive Advertising Campaign" — DoorDash brand presence on LA's bike-share fleet (marketing, not courier mode data).

synthesis_notes: No verified LA-specific courier mode split exists in the public record collected here. The only LA number encountered — '49% of DoorDash LA deliveries on two wheels in 2025' — came from a search-engine summary and could not be found in the DoorDash 2026 report text, the DoorDash 2025 report, or the SVBC write-up; Axios and micromobility.io (the likely carriers) were unreachable. Confidence that the figure is real: low-to-moderate; it must be confirmed before use.

Bounding from verified comparators (DoorDash, two-wheel = bicycle/e-bike/scooter/moped): SF 72%, Santa Clara/Sunnyvale 75%, DC 57%, Philadelphia 35%, San Diego ~33%, Boston/Toronto 32% (2024-2025 data). Given LA's sprawl and a car-dominated Korean-community framing of app delivery, a citywide LA two-wheel share of roughly 25-50% is plausible (medium-low confidence); the dense core (DTLA, Koreatown, Westlake/Pico-Union, USC) is very likely above the citywide figure, but no neighborhood-level data were found.

DoorDash's 'two-wheeled' bucket explicitly includes gas scooters and mopeds, so any LA two-wheel percentage is an upper bound on e-bike+bicycle share; the moped/gas-scooter fraction inside it is unknown. Uber Eats LA offers car / scooter (<50cc, license required) / bike / on foot; DoorDash LA offers car / bicycle and scooter 'depending on your local market' (vehicle background check) — no 'motorcycle' dash type is documented for LA.

Koreatown: Korean restaurants clearly run meaningful volume through Uber Eats/DoorDash/Grubhub (one Korean restaurant: 3,037 Uber Eats orders in 8 months). A parallel Korean-language delivery layer exists (JQS Delivery since 2010, LA 조이퀵서비스, RushOrder app), but its vehicles are undocumented online and its branding (truck emoji, 'LA 전 지역') suggests cars/vans, not Seoul-style 오토바이 riders. No Korean-language rider-recruitment or moped-rental ads surfaced. Confidence that Koreatown has a distinct moped-rider culture: low.

Spanish-language evidence is thin and mostly non-LA: platform pages list auto/bicicleta/scooter/a pie; TikTok 'cuánto gana en moto/bici' content is national. No Westlake/Pico-Union-specific vehicle evidence or informal e-bike/moto rental listings were found in this pass.

Supply-side proxies point to thin dedicated courier-vehicle infrastructure in LA versus SF/NYC: Whizz does not operate in LA; Zoomo's LA status unverified; Craigslist LA shows 55 scooter listings with only 1 explicitly 'delivery' (200cc, $1,699), 50-150cc at $899-$2,795; a NIU electric moped at $2,800. This is consistent with a courier fleet that is mostly personal cars plus owner-purchased e-bikes/scooters rather than rental fleets.
